newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil edges up on India.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil edges up on India.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up late afternoon on Friday after India's unexpectedly large diesel purchase for July delivery but the rise was tampered by the opening of a new arbitrage window from the Mediterranean, traders said.
"The market is up because of India but there are some concerns over the new arbitrage exports from the Med," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.30/$25.35, up about 15 cens from Thursday while July was at $25.15/$25.25 per barrel, up 10 cents from Thursday's quotes, brokers said.
The market first got wind of the bigger India award late Thursday and swaps rose by about 40 cents.
The fresh bullish sentiment also led the establishment of a 15 cents backwardation between the two front months after June/July traded at a five cents contango on Wednesday.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has in its July diesel tender, bought 855,000 tonnes in 19 cargoes, higher than traders initial expectations of between 400,000 tonnes and 600,000 tonnes.

The large award comes as a much needed boost for the market which had over the past month suffered from poor enduser demand with India importing only 315,000 tonnes in June and China cutting back of imports for May and June to under 500,000 tonnes per month due to high stocks and port congestion.
Traders said the new of the bigger India award could lead to firmer Singapore prices which will lead to a new wave of arbitrage exports from the West as the market there is weak.
Already there are signs that traders are looking to ship cargoes from the Med with one 65,000 tonne cargo said fixed for export to the East from the Black Sea.
Traders said prices in the Med are at about $25 per tonne below Singapore with the freight costs at under $20, making it profitable for arbitrage exports.
The fuel oil market rose late afternoon on fresh buying support in the physical market where a new bid was heard at $101.50 per tonne free-on-board Singapore basis.
Traders said the fresh bid coupled with reduced exports from the Middle East is keeping supplies fairly tight.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $100.50/$101.00, up about 75 cents from Thursday.
Traders said news of an explosion in Taiwan's Taoyuan refinery did not sparked any major movements in prices as the damage was restricted to a small fuel oil desulphurization unit.
